warnings:
The Achievement Level bands are fixed against the curriculum, not against the cohort. A child's AL does not depend on how anyone else did. The bands are deliberately uneven — MOE expects slightly under half the cohort to score AL1 to AL4, so the upper bands are narrower. An AL5 covering twenty marks does not mean AL4 is far away.
A cut-off point is the score of the FIRST and LAST student posted to a school in that Posting Group last year. It moves by a few points every year with each cohort's results and choices, and it is a record of what happened rather than a threshold — some students who matched it were tie-broken out and posted elsewhere.
Two MOE pages currently disagree about the second tie-breaker. The Full SBB infographic gives citizenship, then choice order, then ballot; the older results page says choice order does not give priority, but it is describing the 2020 cohort and states that the process changed from 2021. PathAhead encodes the infographic and links both.
A child admitted through Direct School Admission cannot submit the six S1 school choices and cannot transfer. The commitment runs for the duration of the programme, and it is agreed to before PSLE results exist.

warnings:
This is the GROSS aggregate. MOE subtracts bonus points -- up to 4, from CCA grade, English-and-Higher-Mother-Tongue, a Special Programme or Bahasa Indonesia grade, or attending an affiliated JC -- to reach the NET aggregate JAE actually posts on. PathAhead does not collect CCA records or affiliation status, so your real result may be a few points lower (better) than this. The gross figure is the more conservative one to plan around.
L1 is modelled as English Language only. A student offering Higher Mother Tongue may use it as L1 instead if that produces a better aggregate -- MOE computes both and takes the better. PathAhead computes the English-as-L1 version only.
Which subject counts toward R1 (Humanities) versus R2 (Mathematics or Science) versus "other" is PathAhead's own classification of each subject by its ordinary meaning, not a transcription of MOE's official subject-group table. It affects which of YOUR subjects fills which slot, never whether a subject counts, and it is confidence medium.
A Junior College's cut-off range is the L1R5 net aggregate of the first and last student posted to it in the 2027 JAE -- the whole intake, both tails included, from a formula scored on GROSS above. It moves every year, and it is a record of what happened rather than a threshold: some students who matched it were tie-broken out and posted elsewhere.

warnings:
THIS TRANSITION HAS NO COURSE OUTCOMES LOADED, AND CANNOT HAVE ANY YET. The Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise this feeds does not run until 2028 -- no junior college has published a cut-off under it, because none exists. PathAhead computes your aggregate and stops there, rather than showing last cohort's L1R5 ranges next to it: those are a different subject count on a different ceiling, and putting the two side by side would look like a comparison and be nonsense. See SAFEGUARDS.md 4b2.
L1R4 <= 16 (2028) is NOT a rescaled L1R5 <= 20 (2026/2027). Five subjects became four, and the ceiling dropped by more than proportionally. There is no arithmetic that turns one into the other.
Bonus points, CCA-based and otherwise, are not modelled. This is the gross aggregate. All subjects here are assumed taken at G3 -- the G3-to-G2 mapping that matters for the polytechnic transition below does not apply to L1R4, which requires G3 across the board.
The subject-field classification (Humanities / Mathematics-or-Science) carries the same medium-confidence caveat as the 2027 transition.

cases.why: the polytechnic-facing transition: English plus the best 4 remaining, no tag restriction on the second group at all -- the simplest group shape, and the one most likely to be got right by accident if the tagged groups above were wrong

History  C6
steps.detail: only the best 4 count in this group

steps.label: An aggregate of 26 or lower meets the stated requirement. Lower is better.

warnings:
THIS IS AN APPROXIMATION, NOT THE REAL ELR2B2. The actual formula is English plus 2 subjects the DIPLOMA COURSE names as "relevant" plus your 2 remaining best subjects -- and which subjects count as relevant differs by course: an engineering diploma names Mathematics and Physics, a business diploma names Principles of Accounts and Combined Humanities. PathAhead does not hold that per-course list, so it computes English plus your best 4 remaining subjects overall. For most students most of the time this produces the same number, because your best subjects and a course's relevant subjects often overlap -- but it can differ, and the honest thing to do is say so on every screen that shows this figure rather than present it as the number the polytechnic itself would compute.
Bonus points (up to 2, from a CCA grade) are not modelled. This is the gross aggregate.
A polytechnic course's published range is the whole admitted intake -- the lowest and highest ELR2B2 of anyone admitted -- not a middle band. It moves every year, and it is a record of last year's intake rather than a promise about this year's.

school_match_cases.why: nothing set must match every eligible school -- an unfiltered family sees the whole pool

a single filter hides a non-matching school outright. student_sex is set to 'female' purely so the (separately tested) sex-eligibility gate does not mask this case's actual point: a girls' school CHIJ Katong is eligible for a girl, and still fails to match because it is not co-ed

distance_km is informational and drives the shortlist's sort order and the separate km-band filter, never a match dimension here -- this case exists to keep the two engines' haversine arithmetic in agreement, not to test filtering
every 'want' filter engaged at once, against schools that do and do not have each trait

the fix for the 2026-08-13 review finding: a single-sex school must be INELIGIBLE, never merely a non-match, for a student who cannot attend it -- and unconfirmed for a different, clearly stated reason when student_sex is simply not yet known. Checked before any preference filter, independent of every one of them. A postal code is also set here to prove distance_km is populated even for a school this gate has just excluded -- distance is informational and never gated

chij-katong-convent.eligibility_reason: This is a girls school; it does not admit boys. Not a preference to weigh — not a real option for this child.

chij-katong-convent.eligibility_reason: This is a girls school. PathAhead has not been told your child's sex, so it cannot confirm whether this school is even an option — answer that above and this will resolve one way or the other.

school_match_cases.why: the mirror image: 'avoid SAP/IP/Autonomous/Gifted' must match the traits' ABSENCE, not just skip them

within_reach_cases.why: a score comfortably inside the cut-off is in reach
a score exactly cutoff+margin is still in reach -- the margin exists precisely for this case
one point past cutoff+margin is genuinely out of reach

no cutoff held for this school -- whether because it admits through a specialised route, or (the shipped case) because PathAhead does not republish these figures -- must answer None, never False. 'Cannot tell' is not the same claim as 'not in reach'
empty family_groups (score outside the published Posting Group table) must also answer None
a school with PG3/PG2 but no PG1 band -- a family in PG1 must get None for THIS school, not a false negative from a band that was never published
a score that opens a CHOICE between two Posting Groups (family_groups has 2 entries) is in reach if EITHER group's cutoff would admit it -- the family could choose that one

combined_reach_cases.why: the whole range clears the cut-off -- the strongest signal, shown as in-reach
the better (lower) end of the range is in reach but the worse end is not -- 'possible', never plain in-reach, so a caller cannot present it as a match
not in reach anywhere across the range -- the one state a shortlist filter actually hides on
no cut-off held for this school -- must answer unknown, never out-of-reach
an 'upper bound' search is lo_score==hi_score with the same groups at both ends -- this must equal a plain within_reach() call, not a second, subtly different code path
the same degenerate-range identity, one point past the margin -- must be out-of-reach
